name: fold-pre-edit-of-another-case-meets-the-holder-where-the-disk-folds-case
description: Session A takes EXCLUSIVE on data/x.txt; session B then pre-edits DATA/X.TXT. On a case-insensitive disk (caseless) the two spellings open one file, so B meets A's hold exactly as a pre-edit of data/x.txt would: allowed with the collision warning. On a disk that keeps case apart (nfd, none) DATA/X.TXT is another file and B gets the plain {ok: true}: no collision. Both spellings are listed in tracked.yaml, so DATA/X.TXT is tracked on every disk by its own literal pattern; this row cannot tell that admission from an untracked one, which answers the same {ok: true}. Fold 06 is the row that shows the second spelling is its own tracked record there. The warning echoes the path as B sent it, DATA/X.TXT, not the stored data/x.txt. It is compared in full: the holder's short id is derived from A's fixed session id and both timestamps are ISO, which the harness scrubs. Both backends.
